welcome:

bio.summary: Data science can be a catch-all for many tools. My experiences in the statistical, computer science, and business worlds give me the expertise to frame and then tell valuable stories, building the right solutions for the problem at hand. I focus on causal inference, applied ML, and the infrastructure that lets a small team move decisions for billions of users. I strive for technical excellence as well as clear communication to all stakeholders — from engineers to financiers to executives. Every day is an opportunity for learning and growth and to inspire the same in others.
education: B.S. Business and Political Economy + B.A. Computer Science — New York University (Stern + CAS)
Relevant coursework: Big Data Processing, NLP, Data Science for Healthcare, ML Trading Strategies, Agile Development, Data Structures & Algorithms, Negotiations and Consensus Building

highlights: Built foundational tensor engineering infrastructure powering an ML model that predicts customer retention — featurizing a year of 30 time-dependent signals across 700M Windows devices in a single afternoon. Improved team velocity ~1000% (weeks → days for model iteration) and shipped the first model version to see production use for targeted device messaging. Mentored a PhD intern to train the first Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) in the Windows organization.

Designed a novel system for repeatable + interpretable causal analysis, letting data scientists scale insights across hundreds of analysis variations without sacrificing the interpretability needed to act on the results.

Apply ML to forecast Windows monthly active devices and the Windows 10/11 mix for Microsoft executives — supporting critical decision scenarios and fiscal-year target setting for hundreds of downstream metrics.

Analyzed and modeled Windows in-device campaign "noise" and its effect on user retention, quantifying the trade-off between short-term revenue lift and long-term product health. Led to ongoing large-scale investment in tools and models for "right message, right time" and customer campaign fatigue.

Bootstrapped a standardized publishing layer for Windows device data across Microsoft with scalable DataOps, eventually leading a cross-functional team across PM and engineering. Drove a 75% reduction in critical metric pipeline delays, unlocked agentic querying across all Windows datasets, and powered experimentation + targeted campaigns generating hundreds of millions in revenue. As of 2026 it is the most-used data source about Windows devices at Microsoft, producing metrics reported weekly to senior leaders and in public earnings calls.

Modeled expected post-update device health for the Windows 11 rollout using ensemble ML and pattern mining to ensure upgrade stability. Delivered bi-weekly model-interpretation reviews directly to the head of Windows during the Windows 11 launch.
Computed and modeled Windows lifetime value for several key executive decision scenarios around Windows 10 end of support.
Formulated methodology and delivered a POC for first-in-class ML modeling of Azure infrastructure health
COSINE (Core OS & Intelligent Edge) Data Science Team, Azure deployments
Built and maintained data pipelines to automate routine dashboarding
Manipulated 100MM+ rows of data using SQL for user taxonomy project
Classified 900+ advertisements for CTR, CPM, and revenue optimization
Used data analysis to assist advisors in rebalancing $50MM of discretionary client assets
Conducted investment research and advised financial advisors

projects.title: Raspberry Pi Email Summary Agent with Local Processing
projects.description: OpenClaw was an enticing offering, but security and privacy concerns prompted me to explore a local-first approach. I built a Raspberry Pi-based email summary agent that processes data locally and sends me a prioritized digest a few times per day. This project allowed me to experiment with local AI agent capabilities and edge computing while ensuring my data remains private and secure.
projects.status: Public — try it out with the code on my GitHub!

projects.title: wheresmybus — Real-Time Transit from the Terminal
projects.description: I kept missing my bus home from work because I was too deep in AI CLI tools like Claude Code and Copilot CLI. Ironically, I used one to fix the problem. wheresmybus is a Go CLI that gives me real-time King County Metro arrivals without ever leaving the terminal. It auto-detects whether I'm at home or the office via WiFi and shows the right stop — so now I just type `wheresmybus` and never miss the bus again.

projects.title: Agentic Workflows for Time-Series Feature Engineering
projects.description: Designed agentic workflows that assist data scientists with time-series feature engineering for traditional ML at massive scale. The system lets a small team featurize a year of dozens of time-dependent signals across hundreds of millions of devices in an afternoon — collapsing model-iteration cycles from weeks to days and freeing data scientists to focus on higher-level problem framing and model development.

projects.title: Windows Device Semantic Data Model + AI Agents
projects.description: Led ideation and execution of a next-generation semantic data model for Windows device data across Microsoft, modernizing infrastructure that had been in place for over a decade. The platform powers retrieval-augmented (RAG) AI agents over primary Windows data assets and is now the most-used Windows device data source at the company — producing metrics reported weekly to senior leaders and in public earnings calls.

projects.title: ICU Post-Discharge Mortality Prediction
projects.description: Academic project predicting long-term mortality for ICU patients after discharge. Applied classical ML and statistical modeling to clinical time-series data as part of NYU coursework in Data Science for Healthcare.

projects.title: News Topic Modeling + Bias Classification at Scale
projects.description: Academic project modeling topics and classifying political bias across a large news corpus. Built a distributed pipeline on Hadoop and PySpark for ingestion and feature extraction, with an LSTM-based classifier for bias prediction.
